## Highlights
Showing the 12 most recent highlights from 14 user-facing changes.
### New
- On Mac, resting the pointer on a folder in the sidebar lists its tabs, including those in folders inside it, with a search field ready for typing. Open, unload or close a tab there, or drag it out of the folder, without opening the folder. Turn it off in Settings › Appearance › Preview hover. - On iPhone and iPad, holding a tab or pin in the sidebar shows its title, its site and how its page last looked above its menu, and holding a folder, or clicking it with a secondary click, opens a card with its tabs, a search field and the folder's menu behind "…". Hold and move to drag the folder instead. With a pointer on iPad, resting on a tab or folder shows its card beside the sidebar. Turn them off in Settings › Appearance › Previews. - On Mac, choose how long the pointer rests on the window's edge before a hidden sidebar comes out, from Instant to a second, in Settings › Appearance › Sidebar hover delay. It applies in a window and in full screen, and moving off the edge before then still keeps the sidebar hidden. - On Mac, choose how fast the sidebar slides in and out, when it shows from the window's edge and when you hide or dock it, from Snap, which puts it in place at once, to twice as slow as before, in Settings › Appearance › Sidebar slide time. - Turn off Keep saved tabs after unloading in Settings › Tabs and a saved tab you unload shows an X that deletes it. The X waits a moment after you unload the tab, and on iPhone and iPad it always shows rather than on hover. The setting appears in the Heraldic and Modern styles. - Choose how much room the sidebar keeps between tabs, the address field, pins and section headers with Spacing in Settings › Appearance: None, Tight, Default or Relaxed. It appears in every customization style.
### Improved
- Tab size in Settings › Appearance is now a slider with nine steps, from Thin to Large, and a thin tab keeps its title readable while losing the room around it. The Space header grows and shrinks with your tabs. - On Mac, the sidebar slides in and out a third faster by default. Choose its speed in Settings › Appearance › Sidebar slide time.
### Fixed
- The tab list a folder shows when you rest the pointer on it or hold it keeps its text readable with Material color set to Light or Dark. - On Mac, a click anywhere in the sidebar's address field opens it. Clicks above and below "Search or enter website", or an address shown on one line, used to do nothing. - A click anywhere in a Quick Window's address field opens it, including above and below the address or "Search or enter website" and on the lock before it, where clicks used to do nothing. - On Mac, a Quick Window's back and forward buttons draw in the Space's text color, so they stay visible over a dark Space in a light window, or a light Space in a dark one.

## Highlights
### Fixed
- Chromium is updated to 157.0.8103.51, which fixes CVE-2026-125350, a security flaw being exploited in the wild, and eight other security flaws.
---
Stable releases are signed, notarized, and ready for everyday use.

## Highlights
### New
- A new General setting keeps the developer toolbar from opening by itself on local pages. Shift-Command-I still shows it on any page.
### Improved
- Drag the frame around a page on any edge to move the window, as you can from the sidebar. The gap around a floating sidebar moves the window too. Borderless windows have no frame, so every click still reaches the page.
### Fixed
- Full-screen videos in the Chromium engine hide the pointer when you stop moving it, as they do in WebKit. - A page you send from a Quick Window to another Space responds to clicks and typing as soon as it appears, instead of only after you switch tabs. - A hidden sidebar slides out at the window's edge only when that window is in front. Moving the pointer over a window in the background no longer opens its sidebar and leaves it stuck open. - Screen sharing works in Slack huddles and in Slack's call test on pages that run in Chromium. As in Chrome, a site can ask to share your screen without a click of its own, and macOS still asks what to share. - Tabs take the title a page gives itself after it finishes loading. A link you open in the background with Command-click, or a page that shows “Loading…” first, no longer stays named by its address or placeholder. - Pages in Chromium that have no title of their own show the site’s name, as WebKit pages do, instead of their full address. A Chromium tab that reloads in the background keeps its title.
